public class HashMap<A, B>
  extends Map<A, B>
An implementation variant of mappings based on object equality and hash code.

This variant is good suited for mappings which will become relative large. Its efficiency depends on a suitable implementation of the Object.hashCode() method for the domain type of the mapping.

The implementation supports single threadedness w.r.t. to defining and undefining entries, such that in a consecutive sequence of operations 

   map = map.define(x1,y1);
   map = map.undefine(x2);
   map = map.define(x3,y3);
   ...
no copies of the contents of the aggregate are necessary for the intermediate values; thus the complexity is in average O(1+hashCosts).

The implementation uses similar techniques such as HashSet; see there for additional information.

HashMap
public HashMap(int initialCapacity,
               float loadFactor);
Construct an empty hash map with the specified initial capacity and load factor.

Parameters:
initialCapacity - the initial number of buckets
loadFactor - a number between 0.0 and 1.0, it defines the threshold for rehashing the hashtable into a bigger one.
Throws:
IllegalArgumentException -If the initial capacity is less than or equal to zero.
IllegalArgumentException -If the load factor is less than or equal to zero.

HashMap

public HashMap();
Construct an empty hash map.

HashMap

public HashMap(Aggregate<A> other);
Construct a hash map which contains the enumerated elements of another aggregate. This constructor is optimized according to the actual representation of the other aggregate. In particular, if the other aggregate is a hash map again, the new map simply inherits its internal representation.

HashMap

public HashMap(Aggregate<A> dom,
               Aggregate<A> ran);
Construct a hashmap which contains the enumerated elements of one aggregate mapped to the elements of another aggregate. @execption NoSuchElementException if the both aggregates have not the same size.

equals

public boolean equals(Object other);
Test for equality of this hash map with another object. An hash map equals to another object if the other one is an instance of class Map, contains the same number of elements, and each key element of the other set is mapped to the same value in this hash set. Note: currently not implemented because of restricitions of Pizza type casts.

public Enum<Pair<A, B>> enumerate();
Return an enumeration of elements of the mapping, as pairs of domain and codomain values. Each pair is returned exactly once, but the order of enumeration is not determined. As a result, the compare method will not coincides with equality on hashed mappings.
